text: I think education is going to change in a big way. And I think a lot about this because I'm involved in my kid's school quite a bit, and that's something I've done after I left OpenAI.
speaker: Peter Deng
context: Lenny asks Peter what specific thing will change in a big way with AI that people don't think enough about. Peter explains that education will transform dramatically as young people's minds adapt to AI tools. He shares how his nine-year-old son used ChatGPT and other OpenAI models before they were public, and Peter observed how exposure to AI at an early age was literally changing how his son's brain processed information and approached problems.
text_ko: 교육은 앞으로 크게 달라질 거라고 생각해요. 제 아이 학교에 꽤 관여하고 있어서 그 부분에 대해 자주 생각하게 돼요. 그건 OpenAI를 떠난 뒤에 제가 하게 된 일이기도 해요.
text_zh: 我觉得教育会发生很大变化。我经常在想这事，自从离开 OpenAI 后我就经常参与孩子学校的各种事。
text_es: Creo que la educación va a cambiar mucho. Y lo pienso bastante porque estoy muy implicado en la escuela de mi hijo; es algo a lo que me he dedicado desde que dejé OpenAI.
key_sentence: I think education is going to change in a big way.
original_text: I think education is going to change in a big way. And I think a lot about this because I'm involved in my kid's school quite a bit, and that's something I've done after I left OpenAI. And what's fascinating to me is that watching my son who got to dog food, a bunch of the OpenAI stuff before it was public, I think I can safely say that, that seems okay. And when he was playing with ChatGPT and some of the latest models and he was nine at the time, I can already see his brain rewiring.

vocabulary.definition: Being engaged or participating actively in a particular activity or situation; having a role or connection.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being 'involved' often refers to stakeholders or team members who actively contribute to projects, decisions, or organizational processes.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'involved' suggests active participation, it can also imply complexity or entanglement, so it should be used with awareness of the context.

text: Sometimes your product actually doesn't matter. At Uber, I learned this because, really, the price and the ETA at Uber was the product. Looking at it from a holistic perspective, we humans consume the entirety of the product.
speaker: Peter Deng
context: Lenny asks Peter about the most counterintuitive lesson he's learned about building products. Peter shares a hard-learned insight from his time leading the Uber Rider product team - that the digital interface and app features he was optimizing weren't actually the core product. Instead, the real product was the operational elements like pricing and estimated time of arrival, which had much more impact on user satisfaction than any UI improvements.
text_ko: 가끔은 제품(product) 자체가 사실 크게 중요하지 않을 때가 있어요. 우버에서 일하면서 그걸 배웠는데, 사실 우버에선 가격과 도착 예상 시간(ETA)이 바로 제품이었어요. 전체적인 관점(holistic perspective)에서 보면, 사람들은 제품 전체를 경험하고 소비해요.
text_zh: 有时候你的产品其实并不那么重要。我在 Uber 上学到这一点——对用户来说，真正的“产品”是价格和预计到达时间(ETA)。从整体上看，我们消费的其实是整个产品体验。
text_es: A veces tu producto no importa tanto. En Uber lo entendí: el precio y el tiempo estimado de llegada (ETA) eran, de hecho, el producto. Visto en conjunto, las personas consumimos el producto en su totalidad.
key_sentence: Humans consume the entirety of the product, not just fixing bugs.
original_text: Sometimes your product actually doesn't matter. At Uber, I learned this because, really, the price and the ETA at Uber was the product. Looking at it from a holistic perspective, we humans consume the entirety of the product. It's not to say that you shouldn't fix the bug, but it doesn't have as much of an impact as something that is more important to people.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or considering the whole rather than just the parts; an approach that emphasizes the interconnectedness of components within a system.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, a holistic approach might involve integrating various departments to improve overall efficiency and customer satisfaction, rather than optimizing each department in isolation.
vocabulary.nuance: This term conveys a sense of comprehensive understanding and is often used in discussions about strategy, management, and wellness in corporate environments.

vocabulary.definition: A particular attitude or way of regarding something; a point of view that influences how one interprets information or situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding different perspectives is crucial for effective decision-making, as it allows leaders to consider diverse viewpoints and potential impacts on stakeholders.
vocabulary.nuance: This term can imply a subjective interpretation, making it important to clarify whether one is discussing a personal or organizational perspective.

vocabulary.definition: The whole of something; the complete and undivided state of an object or concept.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, considering the entirety of a product or service can lead to better strategic decisions, as it encompasses all aspects that affect customer experience and satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes completeness and is often used in contexts where a full understanding is necessary, such as in assessments or evaluations.

text: You have to plan your chess moves out in advance. You have to really think before you act and build systems that were going to let you go sustainably faster.
speaker: Peter Deng
context: Lenny asks Peter about important lessons for building products from idea to billions of users, drawing on Peter's experience scaling products like Facebook Newsfeed, Messenger, Instagram, and ChatGPT. Peter explains that scaling from one to 100 users requires different thinking than finding initial product-market fit - you must build robust systems and infrastructure that will support rapid growth rather than just moving fast and breaking things.
text_ko: 체스 수(chess moves)를 미리 계획해야 해요. 행동하기 전에 정말 깊이 생각하고, 무리하지 않으면서도 지속적으로 더 빠르게 움직일 수 있게 해주는 시스템(system)을 만들어야 해요.
text_zh: 你得提前把每一步棋都算清楚，别冲动行事，要先想清楚再动手，并搭建能让你长期稳健提速的系统(systems)。
text_es: Debes planear tus jugadas como en una partida de ajedrez: pensar bien antes de actuar y poner en marcha sistemas que te permitan ir más rápido de forma sostenible.
key_sentence: Plan your chess moves out in advance to achieve hyperscale sustainably faster.
original_text: You have to plan your chess moves out in advance. You have to really think before you act and build systems that were going to let you go sustainably faster. Because the zero to one is you're trying to find that product market fit and then when you get to one to 100, you're trying to make sure you can get to hyperscale as fast as you can.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, sustainably often refers to practices that ensure long-term viability and minimal negative impact on the environment, society, and economy.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation, emphasizing responsibility and foresight, and is often used in discussions about corporate social responsibility.

vocabulary.definition: A detailed proposal for achieving specific goals, outlining steps and resources required.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, planning is crucial for setting objectives, allocating resources, and anticipating challenges to ensure successful project execution.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a formal, structured approach, but may also refer to informal strategies; it is essential to distinguish between short-term and long-term planning.

vocabulary.definition: To create structured processes or frameworks that facilitate operations, decision-making, and efficiency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, building systems is vital for streamlining workflows, improving productivity, and ensuring consistency in operations.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase suggests a proactive approach to organizational development and may imply the integration of technology or methodologies to enhance performance.

text: In 6 months, if I'm telling you what to do, I've hired the wrong person. It helps me and the person operate on a different level where the goal is not, did you hit this OKR? The Meta goal becomes, are we calibrating enough?
speaker: Peter Deng
context: Lenny asks Peter what he looks for when hiring people. Peter shares his signature hiring philosophy that has helped him build successful teams across Facebook, Instagram, Uber, OpenAI and other companies. Rather than focusing on specific skills, he optimizes for people who can quickly become autonomous and eventually guide him rather than need constant direction, which creates a meta-goal of developing true partnership rather than just task completion.
text_ko: 6개월쯤 지나서도 제가 계속 뭘 하라고 지시하고 있다면, 사람을 잘못 뽑은 거예요. 그렇게 되면 저랑 그 사람은 다른 수준에서 일하게 되고, 목표가 '이 OKR(OKR)을 달성했냐'가 아니에요. 메타 목표(Meta goal)는 '우리가 충분히 조정(calibrating)하고 있나?'가 돼요.
key_sentence: The meta goal is calibrating enough for the person to lead in 6 months.
original_text: In 6 months, if I'm telling you what to do, I've hired the wrong person. It helps me and the person operate on a different level where the goal is not, did you hit this OKR? The Meta goal becomes, are we calibrating enough? Are we actually getting into a spot where in 6 months you're the one telling me what needs to be done?

vocabulary.definition: The process of adjusting or fine-tuning something to ensure accuracy or optimal performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, calibrating often refers to aligning team objectives, performance metrics, or strategies to ensure that all members are working towards the same goals effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: Calibrating implies a continuous process of adjustment rather than a one-time fix, emphasizing the importance of ongoing evaluation and improvement.

vocabulary.definition: A specific aim or desired outcome that an individual or organization strives to achieve.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, goals are often set to guide strategic planning and measure success, such as sales targets or project completion timelines.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'goal' can refer to both short-term and long-term objectives, it is often associated with measurable outcomes, distinguishing it from broader aspirations.

vocabulary.definition: The act of employing someone for a job or position, typically through a formal recruitment process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and businesses, hiring is crucial for building teams that can drive innovation and achieve company goals, often involving interviews and assessments.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'hired' carries a connotation of selection and approval, indicating that the individual has met specific criteria or expectations.

vocabulary.definition: To function or work in a particular way, often referring to the management or execution of tasks within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, operating effectively means managing resources, processes, and teams to achieve desired outcomes and maintain productivity.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'operate' can imply a level of efficiency and effectiveness, suggesting that the focus is not just on action but on achieving results through structured processes.

text: I think there are five different types of product managers. Number one is the consumer PM. This is the person that's half designer, half product person, really obsessed over the details. Another type is the growth PM.
speaker: Peter Deng
context: Peter shares a framework he developed at Uber for understanding different product manager archetypes. He explains that rather than viewing PM as a single role, there are five distinct types with different natural motivations and skills. He describes consumer PMs who focus on craft and user experience, and growth PMs who are data-driven and skeptical, noting how these different types create healthy tension when working together on teams.
text_ko: 제 생각에 프로덕트 매니저(product manager, PM)는 다섯 가지 유형이 있어요. 첫 번째는 컨슈머(consumer) PM이에요. 이 사람은 반은 디자이너고 반은 프로덕트 담당자라서 세부 사항에 진짜 집착해요. 또 다른 유형은 그로스(growth) PM이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得产品经理（PM）大概有五类。第一类是面向消费者的产品经理（consumer PM），这种人既像设计师又像产品人，对细节特别较真。另一类是负责增长的产品经理（growth PM）。
text_es: Creo que hay cinco tipos distintos de responsables de producto (product managers). El primero es el responsable orientado al consumidor (consumer PM). Es alguien mitad diseñador, mitad profesional de producto (product person), obsesionado con los detalles. Otro tipo es el responsable de crecimiento (growth PM).
key_sentence: I think there are five different types of product managers.
original_text: I think there are five different types of product managers. Number one is the consumer PM. This is the person that's half designer, half product person, really obsessed over the details. Another type is the growth PM. These people are half data scientist, half product person, they are wired to think numbers first and they have this air about them that's like the best ones do, which is like, 'I'm really skeptical. Show me the data.'

vocabulary.definition: Having an excessive preoccupation or fixation on a particular subject or detail.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of product management, being 'obsessed' often refers to a deep commitment to understanding user needs and refining product features to enhance user experience.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'obsessed' can imply a positive dedication, it may also suggest an unhealthy fixation if taken to extremes, so context is crucial.

text: Say you're going to do the thing, say that you're doing the thing, and then say that you did it.
speaker: Peter Deng
context: Lenny asks Peter about management advice he gave to Joanne Jang at OpenAI for managing up more effectively. Peter explains this simple three-part communication framework that helps people stay aligned with their managers and teams. The framework forces intentionality in planning, creates opportunities for course correction during execution, and ensures proper communication of completed work and impact.
text_ko: 할 거라고 미리 알려요, 진행 중이라고 업데이트해요, 끝나면 완료 보고해요.
text_zh: 先说要做，做的时候报个进度，做完了再汇报。
text_es: Di que vas a hacerlo, di que lo estás haciendo y después confirma que ya está hecho.
key_sentence: Say you're going to do the thing, say that you're doing the thing, and then say that you did it.
original_text: Say you're going to do the thing, say that you're doing the thing, and then say that you did it. By giving this phrase to Joanne, maybe it was just like, 'Hey, let's just be very intentional about what we build.' That becomes a constant reminder. And it also has this other effect, where if you're saying, 'This is what I'm doing,' and then that's a thing that your manager's like, 'Wait, we don't need to do that anymore,' you can have a conversation about that.
